subject: Minimal observation for a low CV (in point transect survey)

messages.author: 37e26b419de96fc3
messages.subject: Minimal observation for a low CV (in point transect survey)
parts:
Dear Distance samplers,

I am looking for information of the minimal number of observation for a point transect survey for to have a low CV.
I not find any specific papers for this subject, but maybe some of you discuss this think in one of her papers?

Thank you very much,

Cordially,

Gaël

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Minimal observation for a low CV (in point transect survey)
parts:
Gaël 

It is not a simple calculation to determine CV as a function of sample size for distance sampling.  It depends upon additional factors, such as the variability in number of detections between survey points.

This paper by Prof Buckland describes a detailed songbird study he conducted and provides a comparison of the relative number of hours of effort necessary to achieve desired levels of precision (CV) for different species in his field study.  Perhaps that study may be of use to you.

Buckland, S.T. 2006. Point transect surveys for songbirds: robust methodologies. The Auk 123:345--357   DOI: 10.1642/0004-8038(2006)123[345:PSFSRM]2.0.CO;2

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Minimal observation for a low CV (in point transect survey)
parts:
Gaël

Your mention of Buckland et al. (2001) reminded me of the survey design advice available in Chapter 7 of that book.  Specifically Section 7.2.2.2 helps you decide the amount of survey effort (in terms of number of points) needed to achieve a desired precision.  This approximate calculation is based upon the results of a pilot study where a number of detections (n_0) were made having visited a number of points (k_0).

That is useful for assisting in designing a field survey.
